articles.body: A dog can look convincing in a video and still look wrong when it walks across a desktop. We ran into that while building Mocha Casa, a Windows pet companion made with Electron and JavaScript. This is a development note from our own project. The useful part is the small set of problems behind the demo: synchronizing movement, handling transitions, and giving the user control over a companion that shares their workspace. Start with the relationship, then the controls The intent is to let someone see a familiar pet beside their work, especially when the real dog or cat cannot sit there. That changes the design questions. How much space does it take? How often should it move? Can the user put it away quickly? Our client has a calmer Companion mode and a livelier Active mode.

articles.title: A VIN Validation Checklist for Car Marketplace Developers
articles.excerpt: If you run a car marketplace, classifieds site or dealer tool, the VIN field is your best defense against bad listings, but only if you validate it properly. A check-digit test alone isn't enough. Her…
articles.body: If you run a car marketplace, classifieds site or dealer tool, the VIN field is your best defense against bad listings, but only if you validate it properly. A check-digit test alone isn't enough. Here's a layered checklist, from cheap input checks to cross-checking the listing. 1. Normalize input Trim whitespace, remove spaces and dashes, uppercase everything. Don't silently "fix" I, O and Q to 1/0. Flag them instead: they're never valid in a modern VIN, and auto-correcting can hide typos or fraud. 2. Structural checks (instant, client-side) Exactly 17 characters for vehicles from model year 1981 onward. Allowed alphabet: A-H J-N P R-Z 0-9 . Position 9 check digit passes (North American VINs).

articles.title: VIN Position 11 Deep Dive: Plant Codes, Why They Are Manufacturer-Specific, and How to Use Them
articles.excerpt: Position 11 of a 17-character VIN identifies the assembly plant. It's one of the most useful characters for spotting mismatches and understanding recalls, and also one of the most misunderstood, becau…
articles.body: Position 11 of a 17-character VIN identifies the assembly plant . It's one of the most useful characters for spotting mismatches and understanding recalls, and also one of the most misunderstood, because unlike the model year code it has no universal table . This post explains how it works and how to use it correctly in code and when buying a car. What the standard says Under NHTSA's VIN rule (49 CFR Part 565), position 11 must identify the plant of manufacture, and each manufacturer defines its own plant codes and submits them to NHTSA. ISO 3779 leaves position 11 to the manufacturer too. So the same character means different plants for different makers. A K at position 11 means one factory for one brand and a completely different factory for another.

articles.title: Docker Sandboxes CVE-2026-77179 and CVE-2026-79994: when the agent VM can still reach the host
articles.excerpt: Docker Sandboxes CVE-2026-77179 and CVE-2026-79994: when the agent VM can still reach the host Docker Sandboxes is the feature that runs an AI coding agent inside a purpose-built virtual machine, so t…
articles.body: Docker Sandboxes CVE-2026-77179 and CVE-2026-79994: when the agent VM can still reach the host Docker Sandboxes is the feature that runs an AI coding agent inside a purpose-built virtual machine, so that whatever the agent does stays out of the developer's environment. In September 2026 Docker published two advisories showing that a process inside that virtual machine could reach the host anyway. The virtio-fs path The first issue is CVE-2026-77179. It affects the virtio-fs host server used to share files with the sandbox, in versions from 0.28.0 up to but not including 0.42.0. Docker rated it critical and the CVSS score is 9.4. The scope is macOS, where the shared file system is implemented in this way. The consequence is direct.
